notes: Owner knows patient records are the most important data and that HIPAA applies. Not written down anywhere.
No stated risk appetite. Security spending is decided case by case when something breaks.
The office manager handles IT issues on top of her regular job. The MSP contract doesn't say who owns security decisions.
Has a HIPAA privacy policy from a template. No acceptable use or password policy.
Nobody reviews security status. No reporting from the MSP.
Depends on a cloud practice management vendor and an MSP. No review of their security or contract terms.
No inventory. Staff estimate 18 PCs and 4 laptops. The X-ray imaging PC is not tracked by the MSP.
No risk assessment has ever been done. This project is the first.
No lessons-learned process.
Front desk shares one login. Email has no MFA. Former employees' accounts are not always disabled.
One HIPAA training video at hire. No phishing training.
Practice management data is in the vendor's cloud. Laptops are not encrypted. Local backups go to a USB drive in the server closet.
Most PCs get Windows updates. The imaging PC runs Windows 10 with updates turned off so the imaging software keeps working.
Guest Wi-Fi and office PCs share the same network. One internet connection with no failover.
No log collection. Antivirus is installed but alerts go to an inbox nobody checks.
No one looks at login or firewall events.
No incident response plan. Staff would call the MSP and hope.
No ability to figure out what happened after an incident.
Owner knows breaches must be reported but doesn't know the HIPAA breach notification steps or deadlines.
MSP can reimage a PC. No documented containment steps.
Backups exist but a restore has never been tested.
No plan for telling patients or staff during an outage.
